note: How a compound works in the body, as the screen beside Ask Sig and each fact sheet draw it: where it acts, what changes there, and which blood markers its fact sheet lists may move. Every line comes from the compound's own fact sheet (src: its source numbers there, empty only for a check from the sheet's lab list that the sheet gives no source) and plain physiology; directions are only those the sheet states (up: it says they rise in people; down: it says they may fall in people; watch: it says to check, or the direction comes only from animal or lab studies). Every fact sheet is drawn: HGH, enclomiphene and SS-31 first by hand, then all of them drafted by drawing agents from their sheets, read line by line against each sheet by a separate reviewer, and corrected. scripts/draw_body.md has the rules; scripts/check_body.mjs checks every entry against them and its sheet, in CI. places: the order the screen lines compounds up in, head to toe and then the whole body, with how a sentence names each one. risk: a warning's short name, for the questions to take to a clinician; ask: a question from the fact sheet's "ask your clinician" that joins them; checked: the date of the fact sheet it was drawn from.

hba1c.name: HbA1c

thyroid.name: Thyroid function

phosphate.name: Phosphate

alp.name: Alkaline phosphatase
alp.what: An enzyme from bone and liver.

pth.name: Parathyroid hormone
pth.what: The hormone that keeps calcium and phosphate in balance.

lh.name: LH
lh.what: The pituitary hormone that tells the testes to make testosterone.

fsh.name: FSH
fsh.what: The pituitary hormone that drives sperm production.

testosterone.name: Total testosterone
testosterone.what: Measured in the morning, when it's highest.

estradiol.name: Estradiol
estradiol.what: The main estrogen. Some testosterone turns into it.

hematocrit.name: Hematocrit
hematocrit.what: The share of the blood that's red cells. Too high thickens the blood.

psa.name: PSA
psa.what: A protein made by the prostate.

semen.name: Semen analysis
semen.what: Sperm count and quality, when fertility matters.

eosinophils.name: Eosinophil count
eosinophils.what: A type of white blood cell, counted in a complete blood count with differential. It rises with allergies and with some drugs.

kidney.name: Kidney function
kidney.what: Creatinine and eGFR: how well the kidneys filter the blood. When they filter less, drugs they clear can build up.

lipids.name: Lipid panel
lipids.what: Cholesterol (LDL and HDL) and triglycerides in the blood.

triglycerides.name: Triglycerides
triglycerides.what: A fat carried in the blood, part of the lipid panel.

liver.name: Liver enzymes
liver.what: ALT and AST: they rise when liver cells are stressed or damaged.

potassium.name: Potassium
potassium.what: A mineral the heart and muscles need, kept in a narrow range.

sodium.name: Sodium
sodium.what: The main salt in the blood, kept in a narrow range.

magnesium.name: Magnesium
magnesium.what: A mineral that muscles, nerves and the heart’s rhythm depend on.

calcium.name: Calcium
calcium.what: A mineral in blood and bone, kept in a narrow range.

uricacid.name: Uric acid
uricacid.what: A waste product in the blood; too much can cause gout.

prolactin.name: Prolactin
prolactin.what: The pituitary hormone behind breast milk. Too much can lower sex hormones.

inr.name: INR
inr.what: How long blood takes to clot, checked in people who take warfarin.

cbc.name: Complete blood count
cbc.what: Red cells, white cells and platelets.

ferritin.name: Ferritin
ferritin.what: How much iron the body has stored.

mma.name: Methylmalonic acid
mma.what: It rises when the body is short of B12, so it’s a sensitive check of B12 status.

homocysteine.name: Homocysteine
homocysteine.what: An amino acid that rises when B12 or folate runs low.

vitd.name: Vitamin D
vitd.what: 25-hydroxy vitamin D, the form measured to judge vitamin D status.

ketones.name: Ketones
ketones.what: Made when the body burns fat for fuel. Very high levels make the blood acidic (ketoacidosis).

urineprotein.name: Urine protein
urineprotein.what: Protein in the urine, a sign the kidneys are under strain.

copper.name: Copper
copper.what: A mineral the body needs to make blood cells and keep nerves working.

insulin.name: Fasting insulin
insulin.what: How much insulin is in the blood after a night without food.
